title: Continuous Robust Sound Event Classification Task
author: Ian Mcloughlin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ix3cfqn

steps.title: Create RWCP data directory
steps.instruction: Place the RWCP database into a folder named `data_wav`. Inside `data_wav` create 50 subfolders named exactly as the classes: aircap, bank, bells5, book1, bottle1, bowl, buzzer, candybwl, cap1, case1, cherry1, clap1, clock1, coffcan, coffmill, coin1, crumple, cup1, cymbals, dice1, doorlock, drum, dryer, file, horn, kara, magno1, maracas, mechbell, metal05, pan, particl1, phone1, pipong, pump, punch, ring, sandpp1, saw1, shaver, snap, spray, stapler, sticks, string, teak1, tear, trashbox, whistle1, wood1. In each class subdirectory copy the `.raw` files so that they are named `000.raw.wav` through `079.raw.wav`.

steps.title: Create NOISEX-92 noise directory
steps.instruction: Place the four NOISEX‑92 audio files `babble.wav`, `factory1.wav`, `f16.wav` and `destroyerengine.wav` into a folder named `noisex-92`.

steps.title: Generate testing mixed audio streams
steps.instruction: Run the MATLAB script below to build 100 mixed‑audio streams, each 60 s long, sampled at 16 kHz, using the four NOISEX‑92 noises at an SNR of 0 dB.

substeps.instruction: Loop over class folders (i = 3:52) and over files inside each class (j = 3:82). For each file where `mod(j-3,8) < 3` (select 3 out of every 8 files), increment `ntest`, build the full file path `a = [wav_dir,mydir(i).name,'/',mysubdir(j).name];` and store it in `datadir{ntest}`.
After the loops, randomise the order of the 1500 selected files: `rand('state',0); sq = randperm(1500);`
Choose a random start sample within the 60‑s buffer: `start = ceil(rand() * (fs*t - len + 1));`
Add the audio into the appropriate stream at the random start: `streams(start:start+len-1,i) = streams(start:start+len-1,i) + data;`
After all files are placed, add noise to each stream:
For `j = 1:n` execute `[streams(:,j),noise] = add_noisem(streams(:,j), noise_path{mod(j,4)+1}, SNR, fs);`
Optionally listen to a stream with `sound(streams(:,1),fs);`

steps.title: Create training noisy datasets per SNR
steps.instruction: For each desired signal‑to‑noise ratio (20 dB, 10 dB, 0 dB, –5 dB, –10 dB) create a separate directory (e.g., `data_wav_mix20`, `data_wav_mix10`, `data_wav_mix0`, `data_wav_mix-5`, `data_wav_mix-10`). Inside each of these directories replicate the 50 class subfolders from `data_wav`. Then run a MATLAB mixing routine identical to the one in step 3, but set `SNR` to the target value for that directory before the noise‑addition loop. The script will read each original 80 files per class, place them at random start positions in 60‑s streams (or directly write them back to the class folder), and add the appropriate NOISEX‑92 noise at the specified SNR, preserving the same internal structure.

substeps.instruction: Copy the 50 class subfolders from `data_wav` into the new folder, preserving the `000.raw.wav`‑`079.raw.wav` naming.
Edit the MATLAB script: set `SNR` to the desired level (20, 10, 0, -5, or -10).
Run the script so that each original file is mixed with the selected NOISEX‑92 noise (using the same `noise_path` list) at the chosen SNR.
Verify that each class subfolder now contains the noise‑corrupted versions of the 80 files.
